body.en: The unit circle extends sine, cosine and tangent to all angles and produces periodic graphs.
body.ar: The unit الدائرة extends sine, cosine and tangent to all angles and produces periodic graphs.

body.en: On the unit circle a point is \( (\cos\theta,\sin\theta) \). Radians: \( 180^{\circ}=\pi \). The graphs of \( \sin x \) and \( \cos x \) have period \( 2\pi \); \( \tan x \) has period \( \pi \).
body.ar: On the unit الدائرة a point is \( (\cos\theta,\sin\theta) \). Radians: \( 180^{\circ}=\pi \). The graphs of \( \sin x \) and \( \cos x \) have period \( 2\pi \); \( \tan x \) has period \( \pi \).

body.en: Unit Circle Periodicity, Harmonic Synthesis & Triangle Laws: Every angle \(\theta\) on the unit circle defines \((\cos\theta, \sin\theta)\) with fundamental Pythagorean invariance \(\cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta \equiv 1\). Linear combinations of同-frequency waves \(a\cos\theta \pm b\sin\theta\) collapse into a single phase-shifted sinusoid \(R\cos(\theta \mp \alpha)\) where \(R = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}\) and \(\tan\alpha = b/a\), immediately revealing the exact maximum \(+R\) and minimum \(-R\).
body.ar: Unit الدائرة Periodicity, Harmonic Synthesis & المثلث Laws: Every الزاوية \(\theta\) on the unit الدائرة defines \((\cos\theta, \sin\theta)\) with fundamental Pythagorean invariance \(\cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta \equiv 1\). Linear combinations of同-frequency waves \(a\cos\theta \pm b\sin\theta\) collapse into a single phase-shifted sinusoid \(R\cos(\theta \mp \alpha)\) حيث \(R = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}\) and \(\tan\alpha = b/a\), immediately revealing the exact maximum \(+R\) and minimum \(-R\).

body.en:
Why the Harmonic \(R\)-Formula & Cosine Rule Hold: Expanding \(R\cos(\theta - \alpha)\) via the compound-angle identity gives:

\[ R\cos(\theta - \alpha) = (R\cos\alpha)\cos\theta + (R\sin\alpha)\sin\theta \]

Matching coefficients with \(a\cos\theta + b\sin\theta\) requires \(R\cos\alpha = a\) and \(R\sin\alpha = b\). Squaring and adding yields \(R^2(\cos^2\alpha + \sin^2\alpha) = a^2 + b^2 \implies R = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}\), and dividing gives \(\tan\alpha = \dfrac{b}{a}\).
body.ar:
Why the Harmonic \(R\)-الصيغة & Cosine Rule Hold: Expanding \(R\cos(\theta - \alpha)\) via the compound-الزاوية المتطابقة gives:

\[ R\cos(\theta - \alpha) = (R\cos\alpha)\cos\theta + (R\sin\alpha)\sin\theta \]

Matching المعاملات with \(a\cos\theta + b\sin\theta\) requires \(R\cos\alpha = a\) and \(R\sin\alpha = b\). Squaring and adding yields \(R^2(\cos^2\alpha + \sin^2\alpha) = a^2 + b^2 \implies R = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}\), and dividing gives \(\tan\alpha = \dfrac{b}{a}\).

body.en:
• Radian vs. Degree Conversions: Radians = Degrees \(\times \frac{\pi}{180°}\); Degrees = Radians \(\times \frac{180°}{\pi}\). Ensure your calculator is set to the correct mode for each calculation.
  • Quadrant Signs (ASTC): In Q1 (All positive), Q2 (Sine positive), Q3 (Tangent positive), Q4 (Cosine positive). A negative \(\sin\theta\) must place \(\theta\) in Q3 or Q4.
  • Amplitude vs. Vertical Stretch: For \(y = A\sin(Bx)\), the amplitude is strictly non-negative: \(|A|\). A negative coefficient (e.g. \(-3\sin x\)) indicates a vertical reflection, but the amplitude remains \(3\).
  • Period of Tangent vs. Sine/Cosine: The period of \(\sin(Bx)\) and \(\cos(Bx)\) is \(\frac{2\pi}{|B|}\). However, the period of \(\tan(Bx)\) is \(\frac{\pi}{|B|}\). Do not use \(2\pi\) for tangent!
body.ar:
• Radian vs. Degree Conversions: Radians = Degrees \(\times \frac{\pi}{180°}\); Degrees = Radians \(\times \frac{180°}{\pi}\). Ensure your calculator is set to the correct mode for each calculation.
  • Quadrant Signs (ASTC): In Q1 (All positive), Q2 (Sine positive), Q3 (Tangent positive), Q4 (Cosine positive). A negative \(\sin\theta\) must place \(\theta\) in Q3 or Q4.
  • Amplitude vs. Vertical Stretch: For \(y = A\sin(Bx)\), the amplitude is strictly non-negative: \(|A|\). A negative المعامل (e.g. \(-3\sin x\)) indicates a vertical reflection, but the amplitude remains \(3\).
  • Period of Tangent vs. Sine/Cosine: The period of \(\sin(Bx)\) and \(\cos(Bx)\) is \(\frac{2\pi}{|B|}\). However, the period of \(\tan(Bx)\) is \(\frac{\pi}{|B|}\). Do not use \(2\pi\) for tangent!

body.en:
Problem (Hard): What is the maximum value of the function \[ f(x) = \sqrt{3}\sin(2x) - \cos(2x) - 2\sin x + 2\sqrt{3}\cos x \] for all real numbers \( x \)?

Step-by-Step Solution: We solve the problem by synthesizing harmonic form (linear combination of sine and cosine), angle-doubling relationships, and quadratic optimization on a restricted domain. **Step 1: Express the single-angle terms in harmonic form.** Recall the linear combination identity \( A\cos x + B\sin x = R\cos(x - \alpha) \). For the terms \( 2\sqrt{3}\cos x - 2\sin x \): \[ 2\sqrt{3}\cos x - 2\sin x = 4\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cos x - \frac{1}{2}\sin x\right) \] Using the cosine addition formula \( \cos(A + B) = \cos A \cos B - \sin A \sin B \) with \( \cos\frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \) and \( \sin\frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{1}{2} \): \[ 2\sqrt{3}\cos x - 2\sin x = 4\cos\left(x + \frac{\pi}{6}\right) \] **Step 2: Express the double-angle terms using the same phase angle.** For \( \sqrt{3}\sin(2x) - \cos(2x) \): \[ \sqrt{3}\sin(2x) - \cos(2x) = -\left(\cos(2x) - \sqrt{3}\sin(2x)\right) = -2\left(\frac{1}{2}\cos(2x) - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\sin(2x)\right) \] Recognizing \( \cos\frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{1}{2} \) and \( \sin\frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \): \[ \sqrt{3}\sin(2x) - \cos(2x) = -2\cos\left(2x + \frac{\pi}{3}\right) \] **Step 3: Relate the arguments.** Notice that the argument of the double-angle cosine is exactly twice that of the single-angle cosine: \[ 2x + \frac{\pi}{3} = 2\left(x + \frac{\pi}{6}\right) \] Letting \( \theta = x + \frac{\pi}{6} \), the function simplifies to: \[ f(x) = -2\cos(2\theta) + 4\cos\theta \] **Step 4: Convert to a quadratic in \( \cos\theta \).** Using the double-angle identity \( \cos(2\theta) = 2\cos^2\theta - 1 \): \[ f(x) = -2(2\cos^2\theta - 1) + 4\cos\theta = -4\cos^2\theta + 4\cos\theta + 2 \] **Step 5: Optimize over the domain.** Let \( u = \cos\theta \). Because \( x \in \mathbb{R} \), \( u \) takes all values in the interval \( [-1, 1] \). We maximize the quadratic function: \[ g(u) = -4u^2 + 4u + 2 \] Completing the square: \[ g(u) = -4\left(u^2 - u\right) + 2 = -4\left(u - \frac{1}{2}\right)^2 + 4\left(\frac{1}{4}\right) + 2 = -4\left(u - \frac{1}{2}\right)^2 + 3 \] The vertex occurs at \( u = \frac{1}{2} \). Since \( \frac{1}{2} \in [-1, 1] \), the maximum is achievable (for example, when \( x + \frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{\pi}{3} \implies x = \frac{\pi}{6} \)) and is equal to \( 3 \). **Misconception Analysis:** - **Choice B (2):** Occurs if one incorrectly assumes the maximum must happen at the boundary \( u = 1 \), giving \( -4(1)^2 + 4(1) + 2 = 2 \). - **Choice C (6):** Occurs from the naive triangle inequality / peak addition \( |{-2}| + |4| = 6 \), ignoring that the two harmonic waves cannot peak at the same \( x \). - **Choice D (1):** Occurs from dropping the constant term \( +1 \) when substituting the identity \( \cos(2\theta) = 2\cos^2\theta - 1 \).
body.ar:
Problem (Hard): What is the maximum value of the الدالة \[ f(x) = \sqrt{3}\sin(2x) - \cos(2x) - 2\sin x + 2\sqrt{3}\cos x \] for all real numbers \( x \)?

Step-by-Step الحل: We solve the problem by synthesizing harmonic form (linear combination of sine and cosine), الزاوية-doubling relationships, and quadratic optimization on a restricted المجال. **الخطوة ١: Express the single-الزاوية terms in harmonic form.** Recall the linear combination المتطابقة \( A\cos x + B\sin x = R\cos(x - \alpha) \). For the terms \( 2\sqrt{3}\cos x - 2\sin x \): \[ 2\sqrt{3}\cos x - 2\sin x = 4\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cos x - \frac{1}{2}\sin x\right) \] Using the cosine addition الصيغة \( \cos(A + B) = \cos A \cos B - \sin A \sin B \) with \( \cos\frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \) and \( \sin\frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{1}{2} \): \[ 2\sqrt{3}\cos x - 2\sin x = 4\cos\left(x + \frac{\pi}{6}\right) \] **الخطوة ٢: Express the double-الزاوية terms using the same phase الزاوية.** For \( \sqrt{3}\sin(2x) - \cos(2x) \): \[ \sqrt{3}\sin(2x) - \cos(2x) = -\left(\cos(2x) - \sqrt{3}\sin(2x)\right) = -2\left(\frac{1}{2}\cos(2x) - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\sin(2x)\right) \] Recognizing \( \cos\frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{1}{2} \) and \( \sin\frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \): \[ \sqrt{3}\sin(2x) - \cos(2x) = -2\cos\left(2x + \frac{\pi}{3}\right) \] **الخطوة ٣: Relate the arguments.** Notice that the argument of the double-الزاوية cosine is exactly twice that of the single-الزاوية cosine: \[ 2x + \frac{\pi}{3} = 2\left(x + \frac{\pi}{6}\right) \] Letting \( \theta = x + \frac{\pi}{6} \), the الدالة simplifies to: \[ f(x) = -2\cos(2\theta) + 4\cos\theta \] **الخطوة ٤: Convert to a quadratic in \( \cos\theta \).** Using the double-الزاوية المتطابقة \( \cos(2\theta) = 2\cos^2\theta - 1 \): \[ f(x) = -2(2\cos^2\theta - 1) + 4\cos\theta = -4\cos^2\theta + 4\cos\theta + 2 \] **الخطوة ٥: Optimize over the المجال.** Let \( u = \cos\theta \). Because \( x \in \mathbb{R} \), \( u \) takes all values in the interval \( [-1, 1] \). We maximize the quadratic الدالة: \[ g(u) = -4u^2 + 4u + 2 \] Completing the square: \[ g(u) = -4\left(u^2 - u\right) + 2 = -4\left(u - \frac{1}{2}\right)^2 + 4\left(\frac{1}{4}\right) + 2 = -4\left(u - \frac{1}{2}\right)^2 + 3 \] The الرأس occurs at \( u = \frac{1}{2} \). Since \( \frac{1}{2} \in [-1, 1] \), the maximum is achievable (for example, عندما \( x + \frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{\pi}{3} \implies x = \frac{\pi}{6} \)) and is equal to \( 3 \). **Misconception Analysis:** - **Choice B (2):** Occurs if one incorrectly assumes the maximum must happen at the boundary \( u = 1 \), giving \( -4(1)^2 + 4(1) + 2 = 2 \). - **Choice C (6):** Occurs from the naive المثلث المتباينة / peak addition \( |{-2}| + |4| = 6 \), ignoring that the two harmonic waves cannot peak at the same \( x \). - **Choice D (1):** Occurs from dropping the الثابت term \( +1 \) عندما substituting the المتطابقة \( \cos(2\theta) = 2\cos^2\theta - 1 \).

body.en:
Problem (Easy): What is the period of the trigonometric function \(f(x) = 5\cos(4x) - 2\)?

Step-by-Step Solution: For a sinusoidal function written in the standard form \(f(x) = A\cos(Bx - C) + D\), the period \(T\) is determined by the coefficient of \(x\): \[T = \frac{2\pi}{|B|}\] For the given function \(f(x) = 5\cos(4x) - 2\), the frequency coefficient is \(B = 4\). Substituting this into the period formula gives: \[T = \frac{2\pi}{4} = \frac{\pi}{2}\] Misconception analysis: - \(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\) results from incorrectly applying the period formula for the tangent function, \(\frac{\pi}{|B|}\). - \(2\pi\) is the period of the parent function \(y = \cos(x)\), neglecting the horizontal compression caused by \(B = 4\). - \(8\pi\) results from mistakenly multiplying the base period \(2\pi\) by \(4\) rather than dividing.
body.ar:
Problem (Easy): What is the period of the trigonometric الدالة \(f(x) = 5\cos(4x) - 2\)?

Step-by-Step الحل: For a sinusoidal الدالة written in the standard form \(f(x) = A\cos(Bx - C) + D\), the period \(T\) is determined by the المعامل of \(x\): \[T = \frac{2\pi}{|B|}\] For the المعطيات الدالة \(f(x) = 5\cos(4x) - 2\), the frequency المعامل is \(B = 4\). Substituting this into the period الصيغة gives: \[T = \frac{2\pi}{4} = \frac{\pi}{2}\] Misconception analysis: - \(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\) results from incorrectly applying the period الصيغة for the tangent الدالة, \(\frac{\pi}{|B|}\). - \(2\pi\) is the period of the parent الدالة \(y = \cos(x)\), neglecting the horizontal compression caused by \(B = 4\). - \(8\pi\) results from mistakenly multiplying the base period \(2\pi\) by \(4\) rather than dividing.

question.en: If \(\sin\theta = -\frac{4}{5}\) and \(\theta\) lies in Quadrant III, find the exact values of \(\cos\theta\), \(\tan\theta\), and \(\sin(2\theta)\).
question.ar: إذا كان \(\sin\theta = -\frac{4}{5}\) and \(\theta\) lies in Quadrant III, أوجد exact values of \(\cos\theta\), \(\tan\theta\), and \(\sin(2\theta)\).

solution.en:
Using the Pythagorean identity \(\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1\):

\[\left(-\frac{4}{5}\right)^2 + \cos^2\theta = 1 \implies \frac{16}{25} + \cos^2\theta = 1 \implies \cos^2\theta = \frac{9}{25}.\]

Since \(\theta\) is in Quadrant III, cosine is negative: \[\cos\theta = -\frac{3}{5}.\]

Tangent is positive in Quadrant III: \[\tan\theta = \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta} = \frac{-4/5}{-3/5} = \frac{4}{3}.\]

Double-angle formula for sine: \[\sin(2\theta) = 2\sin\theta\cos\theta = 2\left(-\frac{4}{5}\right)\left(-\frac{3}{5}\right) = \frac{24}{25}.\]
solution.ar:
باستخدام Pythagorean identity \(\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1\):

\[\left(-\frac{4}{5}\right)^2 + \cos^2\theta = 1 \implies \frac{16}{25} + \cos^2\theta = 1 \implies \cos^2\theta = \frac{9}{25}.\]

Since \(\theta\) is in Quadrant III, cosine is negative: \[\cos\theta = -\frac{3}{5}.\]

Tangent is positive in Quadrant III: \[\tan\theta = \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta} = \frac{-4/5}{-3/5} = \frac{4}{3}.\]

Double-angle formula for sine: \[\sin(2\theta) = 2\sin\theta\cos\theta = 2\left(-\frac{4}{5}\right)\left(-\frac{3}{5}\right) = \frac{24}{25}.\]

hints.en: Since \(\theta\) is in Quadrant III, cosine is negative: \(\cos\theta = -\frac{3}{5}\) Tangent is positive in Quadrant III: \(\tan\theta = \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta} = \frac{-4/5}{-3/5}\).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(\theta\) ، \(\cos\theta = -\frac{3}{5}\) ، \(\tan\theta = \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta} = \frac{-4/5}{-3/5}\) لتبسيط الخطوة.
تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(\sin(2\theta) = 2\sin\theta\cos\theta = 2\left(-\frac{4}{5}\right)\left(-\frac{3}{5}\right)\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

question.en: [Practice 3 · Medium] Consider the function \[ f(x) = 4\cos^2(x) + b\sin(x) + c \] where \( b \) and \( c \) are real constants with \( b > 0 \). If the maximum value of \( f(x) \) is \( 10 \) and the minimum value of \( f(x) \) is \( 1 \), what is the value of \( c \)?
question.ar: [Practice 3 · Medium] Consider the function \[ f(x) = 4\cos^2(x) + b\sin(x) + c \] حيث \( b \) and \( c \) are real constants with \( b > 0 \). إذا كان the maximum value of \( f(x) \) is \( 10 \) and the minimum value of \( f(x) \) is \( 1 \), ما قيمة \( c \)?

hints.en: To find the unknown parameters, we first express \( f(x) \) in terms of a single trigonometric function using the identity \( \cos^2(x) = 1 - \sin^2(x) \): \(f(x) = 4(1 - \sin^2(x)) + b\sin(x) + c = -4\sin^2(x) + b\sin(x) + c + 4\).
hints.ar: To أوجد unknown parameters, we first express \( f(x) \) in terms of a single trigonometric function باستخدام identity \( \cos^2(x) = 1 - \sin^2(x) \): \(f(x) = 4(1 - \sin^2(x)) + b\sin(x) + c = -4\sin^2(x) + b\sin(x) + c + 4\).

hints.en: Because the vertex \( u_v = \frac{b}{8} > 0 \) is closer to \( 1 \) than to \( -1 \), the point in \( [-1, 1] \) farthest from the vertex is \( u = -1 \). Thus, the minimum value occurs at \( u = -1 \): \(g(-1) = -4(-1)^2 + b(-1) + c + 4 = c - b\).
hints.ar: Because the vertex \( u_v = \frac{b}{8} > 0 \) is closer to \( 1 \) than to \( -1 \), the point in \( [-1, 1] \) farthest from the vertex is \( u = -1 \). وعليه، the minimum value occurs at \( u = -1 \): \(g(-1) = -4(-1)^2 + b(-1) + c + 4 = c - b\).

hints.en: If \(u_v > 1\), \(g(u)\) is strictly increasing on \([-1, 1]\). The maximum would be at \(u = 1\) (giving \(b + c = 10\)) and the minimum at \(u = -1\) (giving \(c - b = 1\)). Solving this system yields \(c = \frac{11}{2}\) and \(b = \frac{9}{2}\), which contradicts \(b > 8\).
hints.ar: إذا كان \(u_v > 1\), \(g(u)\) is strictly increasing on \([-1, 1]\). The maximum would be at \(u = 1\) (giving \(b + c = 10\)) and the minimum at \(u = -1\) (giving \(c - b = 1\)). Solving this system yields \(c = \frac{11}{2}\) and \(b = \frac{9}{2}\), which contradicts \(b > 8\).

solution.en:
To find the unknown parameters, we first express \( f(x) \) in terms of a single trigonometric function using the identity \( \cos^2(x) = 1 - \sin^2(x) \):
\[ f(x) = 4(1 - \sin^2(x)) + b\sin(x) + c = -4\sin^2(x) + b\sin(x) + c + 4 \]

Let \( u = \sin(x) \). Since \( x \in \mathbb{R} \), the variable \( u \) is restricted to the interval \( [-1, 1] \). We analyze the quadratic function:
\[ g(u) = -4u^2 + bu + c + 4, \quad u \in [-1, 1] \]

The graph of \( g(u) \) is a downward-opening parabola with its vertex at:
\[ u_v = -\frac{b}{2(-4)} = \frac{b}{8} \]

Since \( b > 0 \), the vertex position satisfies \( u_v > 0 \).

**Case 1: The vertex lies within the domain (\( 0 < b \le 8 \))**
If \( 0 < \frac{b}{8} \le 1 \), the maximum value occurs at the vertex \( u = \frac{b}{8} \):
\[ g\left(\frac{b}{8}\right) = -4\left(\frac{b}{8}\right)^2 + b\left(\frac{b}{8}\right) + c + 4 = \frac{b^2}{16} + c + 4 \]
Setting the maximum equal to \( 10 \):
\[ \frac{b^2}{16} + c + 4 = 10 \implies \frac{b^2}{16} + c = 6 \quad \text{--- (1)} \]

Because the vertex \( u_v = \frac{b}{8} > 0 \) is closer to \( 1 \) than to \( -1 \), the point in \( [-1, 1] \) farthest from the vertex is \( u = -1 \). Thus, the minimum value occurs at \( u = -1 \):
\[ g(-1) = -4(-1)^2 + b(-1) + c + 4 = c - b \]
Setting the minimum equal to \( 1 \):
\[ c - b = 1 \implies c = b + 1 \quad \text{--- (2)} \]

Substitute equation (2) into equation (1):
\[ \frac{b^2}{16} + (b + 1) = 6 \implies b^2 + 16b - 80 = 0 \]
Factoring gives:
\[ (b + 20)(b - 4) = 0 \]
Since \( b > 0 \), we have \( b = 4 \). Checking the condition, \( u_v = \frac{4}{8} = \frac{1}{2} \in [-1, 1] \), which is valid.
Then, \( c = b + 1 = 4 + 1 = 5 \).

**Case 2: The vertex lies outside the domain (\( b > 8 \))**
If \( u_v > 1 \), \( g(u) \) is strictly increasing on \( [-1, 1] \). The maximum would be at \( u = 1 \) (giving \( b + c = 10 \)) and the minimum at \( u = -1 \) (giving \( c - b = 1 \)). Solving this system yields \( c = \frac{11}{2} \) and \( b = \frac{9}{2} = 4.5 \), which contradicts \( b > 8 \).

Therefore, \( c = 5 \).

*Common misconceptions:*
- Assuming the maximum must occur at the boundary \( \sin(x) = 1 \) without checking the vertex gives \( c = \frac{11}{2} \).
- Forgetting to distribute the factor \( 4 \) to the constant term when substituting \( \cos^2(x) = 1 - \sin^2(x) \) leads to \( c = 9 \).
- Confusing the required parameter \( c \) with \( b \) yields \( 4 \).
solution.ar:
To أوجد unknown parameters, we first express \( f(x) \) in terms of a single trigonometric function باستخدام identity \( \cos^2(x) = 1 - \sin^2(x) \):
\[ f(x) = 4(1 - \sin^2(x)) + b\sin(x) + c = -4\sin^2(x) + b\sin(x) + c + 4 \]

ليكن \( u = \sin(x) \). Since \( x \in \mathbb{R} \), the variable \( u \) is restricted to the interval \( [-1, 1] \). We analyze the quadratic function:
\[ g(u) = -4u^2 + bu + c + 4, \quad u \in [-1, 1] \]

The graph of \( g(u) \) is a downward-opening parabola with its vertex at:
\[ u_v = -\frac{b}{2(-4)} = \frac{b}{8} \]

Since \( b > 0 \), the vertex position satisfies \( u_v > 0 \).

**Case 1: The vertex lies within the domain (\( 0 < b \le 8 \))**
إذا كان \( 0 < \frac{b}{8} \le 1 \), the maximum value occurs at the vertex \( u = \frac{b}{8} \):
\[ g\left(\frac{b}{8}\right) = -4\left(\frac{b}{8}\right)^2 + b\left(\frac{b}{8}\right) + c + 4 = \frac{b^2}{16} + c + 4 \]
Setting the maximum equal to \( 10 \):
\[ \frac{b^2}{16} + c + 4 = 10 \implies \frac{b^2}{16} + c = 6 \quad \text{--- (1)} \]

Because the vertex \( u_v = \frac{b}{8} > 0 \) is closer to \( 1 \) than to \( -1 \), the point in \( [-1, 1] \) farthest from the vertex is \( u = -1 \). وعليه، the minimum value occurs at \( u = -1 \):
\[ g(-1) = -4(-1)^2 + b(-1) + c + 4 = c - b \]
Setting the minimum equal to \( 1 \):
\[ c - b = 1 \implies c = b + 1 \quad \text{--- (2)} \]

عوّض equation (2) into equation (1):
\[ \frac{b^2}{16} + (b + 1) = 6 \implies b^2 + 16b - 80 = 0 \]
حلّلing gives:
\[ (b + 20)(b - 4) = 0 \]
Since \( b > 0 \), we have \( b = 4 \). Checking the condition, \( u_v = \frac{4}{8} = \frac{1}{2} \in [-1, 1] \), which is valid.
Then, \( c = b + 1 = 4 + 1 = 5 \).

**Case 2: The vertex lies outside the domain (\( b > 8 \))**
إذا كان \( u_v > 1 \), \( g(u) \) is strictly increasing on \( [-1, 1] \). The maximum would be at \( u = 1 \) (giving \( b + c = 10 \)) and the minimum at \( u = -1 \) (giving \( c - b = 1 \)). Solving this system yields \( c = \frac{11}{2} \) and \( b = \frac{9}{2} = 4.5 \), which contradicts \( b > 8 \).

وبالتالي، \( c = 5 \).

*Common misconceptions:*
- Assuming the maximum must occur at the boundary \( \sin(x) = 1 \) without checking the vertex gives \( c = \frac{11}{2} \).
- Forgetting to distribute the حلّل \( 4 \) to the constant term عندما substituting \( \cos^2(x) = 1 - \sin^2(x) \) leads to \( c = 9 \).
- Confباستخدام required parameter \( c \) with \( b \) yields \( 4 \).

question.en: [Practice 4 · Hard] Which describes a vertical stretch of \(y=f(x)\) by factor 4?
question.ar: [Practice 4 · Hard] Which describes a vertical stretch of \(y=f(x)\) by حلّل 4?

hints.en: A vertical stretch of a function \(y = f(x)\) scales all output \(y\)-values away from the \(x\)-axis.
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \(y = f(x)\) ، \(y\) ، \(x\) لتبسيط الخطوة.

hints.en: Multiplying the outside of the function by a constant factor \(c > 1\) gives the transformed equation \(y = c\,f(x)\).
hints.ar: Multiplying the outside of the function by a constant حلّل \(c > 1\) gives the transformed equation \(y = c\,f(x)\).

hints.en: For a vertical stretch by factor \(4\), multiply the output by \(4\) to get \(y = 4f(x)\).
hints.ar: For a vertical stretch by حلّل \(4\), multiply the output by \(4\) to get \(y = 4f(x)\).

solution.en: A vertical stretch of a function \(y = f(x)\) scales all output \(y\)-values away from the \(x\)-axis. Multiplying the outside of the function by a constant factor \(c > 1\) gives the transformed equation \(y = c\,f(x)\). For a vertical stretch by factor \(4\), multiply the output by \(4\) to get \(y = 4f(x)\).

Multiplying the outside of the function by a constant حلّل \(c > 1\) gives the transformed equation \(y = c\,f(x)\). For a vertical stretch by حلّل \(4\), multiply the output by \(4\) to get \(y = 4f(x)\).

question.en: [Practice 5 · Easy] In the \(xy\)-plane, an angle \(\theta\) is in standard position. If the terminal side of \(\theta\) passes through the point \((-5, 12)\), what is the value of \(\sin(\theta)\)?
question.ar: [Practice 5 · Easy] In the \(xy\)-plane, an angle \(\theta\) is in standard position. إذا كان the terminal side of \(\theta\) يمر بالنقطة the point \((-5, 12)\), ما قيمة \(\sin(\theta)\)?

hints.en: To find \(\sin(\theta)\) for an angle in standard position whose terminal side passes through \((x, y) = (-5, 12)\): 1. Calculate the distance \(r\) from the origin to the point:.
hints.ar: To أوجد \(\sin(\theta)\) for an angle in standard position whose terminal side يمر بالنقطة \((x, y) = (-5, 12)\): 1. احسب distance \(r\) from the origin to the point:.

hints.en: Rewrite and simplify to obtain: \(r = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2} = \sqrt{(-5)^2 + 12^2} = \sqrt{25 + 144} = \sqrt{169}\).
hints.ar: أعد كتابة العلاقة وبسّطها للحصول على: \(r = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2} = \sqrt{(-5)^2 + 12^2} = \sqrt{25 + 144} = \sqrt{169}\).

hints.en: By the coordinate definition of trigonometric functions: \(\sin(\theta) = \frac{y}{r}\).
hints.ar: بتطبيق coordinate definition of trigonometric functions: \(\sin(\theta) = \frac{y}{r}\).

solution.en:
To find \(\sin(\theta)\) for an angle in standard position whose terminal side passes through \((x, y) = (-5, 12)\):

1. Calculate the distance \(r\) from the origin to the point:
\[ r = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2} = \sqrt{(-5)^2 + 12^2} = \sqrt{25 + 144} = \sqrt{169} = 13 \]

2. By the coordinate definition of trigonometric functions:
\[ \sin(\theta) = \frac{y}{r} = \frac{12}{13} \]

Misconception checks:
- \(-\frac{5}{13}\) results from confusing sine with cosine, where \(\cos(\theta) = \frac{x}{r}\).
- \(-\frac{12}{13}\) comes from mistakenly assigning a negative sign in Quadrant II, where the \(y\)-coordinate and sine are actually positive.
- \(-\frac{12}{5}\) is \(\tan(\theta) = \frac{y}{x}\).
solution.ar:
To أوجد \(\sin(\theta)\) for an angle in standard position whose terminal side يمر بالنقطة \((x, y) = (-5, 12)\):

1. احسب distance \(r\) from the origin to the point:
\[ r = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2} = \sqrt{(-5)^2 + 12^2} = \sqrt{25 + 144} = \sqrt{169} = 13 \]

2. بتطبيق coordinate definition of trigonometric functions:
\[ \sin(\theta) = \frac{y}{r} = \frac{12}{13} \]

Misconception checks:
- \(-\frac{5}{13}\) results from confusing sine with cosine, حيث \(\cos(\theta) = \frac{x}{r}\).
- \(-\frac{12}{13}\) comes from mistakenly assigning a negative sign in Quadrant II, حيث the \(y\)-coordinate and sine are actually positive.
- \(-\frac{12}{5}\) is \(\tan(\theta) = \frac{y}{x}\).

label.en: ● Complete Guide to All 6 Trigonometric Ratios — Unit Circle, Reciprocals, Domains, Periods & Asymptotes
label.ar: ● الدليل الشامل للنسب المثلثية الست — دائرة الوحدة والمقلوبات والمجالات والدورات وخطوط التقارب

body.en:
For any angle \( heta\) in standard position whose terminal ray intersects the unit circle \(x^2 + y^2 = 1\) at \(P(\cos heta, \sin heta)\) (or a right triangle with opposite \(o\), adjacent \(a\), and hypotenuse \(h\)), the six trigonometric functions are:

\[ \sin heta = y = rac{o}{h}, \qquad \cos heta = x = rac{a}{h}, \qquad an heta = rac{\sin heta}{\cos heta} = rac{y}{x} = rac{o}{a} \]\[ \csc heta = rac{1}{\sin heta} = rac{h}{o}, \qquad \sec heta = rac{1}{\cos heta} = rac{h}{a}, \qquad \cot heta = rac{\cos heta}{\sin heta} = rac{x}{y} = rac{a}{o} \]
FunctionDomainRangePeriodSymmetryVertical Asymptotes
\(\sin heta\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([-1, 1]\)\(2\pi\)OddNone
\(\cos heta\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([-1, 1]\)\(2\pi\)EvenNone
\( an heta\)\( heta eq rac{\pi}{2} + k\pi\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\(\pi\)Odd\( heta = rac{\pi}{2} + k\pi\)
\(\csc heta\)\( heta eq k\pi\)\((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\)\(2\pi\)Odd\( heta = k\pi\)
\(\sec heta\)\( heta eq rac{\pi}{2} + k\pi\)\((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\)\(2\pi\)Even\( heta = rac{\pi}{2} + k\pi\)
\(\cot heta\)\( heta eq k\pi\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\(\pi\)Odd\( heta = k\pi\)

Pythagorean Identities: \(\sin^2 heta + \cos^2 heta = 1\), \(1 + an^2 heta = \sec^2 heta\), and \(1 + \cot^2 heta = \csc^2 heta\).
body.ar:
لأي زاوية \( heta\) في الوضع القياسي يقطع ضلع انتهائها دائرة الوحدة \(x^2 + y^2 = 1\) عند النقطة \(P(\cos heta, \sin heta)\) (أو في مثلث قائم الزاوية بمقابل \(o\) ومجاور \(a\) ووتر \(h\))، تُعرَّف الدوال المثلثية الست كما يلي:

\[ \sin heta = y = rac{o}{h}, \qquad \cos heta = x = rac{a}{h}, \qquad an heta = rac{\sin heta}{\cos heta} = rac{y}{x} = rac{o}{a} \]\[ \csc heta = rac{1}{\sin heta} = rac{h}{o}, \qquad \sec heta = rac{1}{\cos heta} = rac{h}{a}, \qquad \cot heta = rac{\cos heta}{\sin heta} = rac{x}{y} = rac{a}{o} \]
الدالةالمجالالمدىالدورة الأساسيةالتماثلخطوط التقارب الرأسية
\(\sin heta\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([-1, 1]\)\(2\pi\)فرديةلا يوجد
\(\cos heta\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([-1, 1]\)\(2\pi\)زوجيةلا يوجد
\( an heta\)\( heta eq rac{\pi}{2} + k\pi\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\(\pi\)فردية\( heta = rac{\pi}{2} + k\pi\)
\(\csc heta\)\( heta eq k\pi\)\((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\)\(2\pi\)فردية\( heta = k\pi\)
\(\sec heta\)\( heta eq rac{\pi}{2} + k\pi\)\((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\)\(2\pi\)زوجية\( heta = rac{\pi}{2} + k\pi\)
\(\cot heta\)\( heta eq k\pi\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\(\pi\)فردية\( heta = k\pi\)

متطابقات فيثاغورس المثلثية: \(\sin^2 heta + \cos^2 heta = 1\)، و\(1 + an^2 heta = \sec^2 heta\)، و\(1 + \cot^2 heta = \csc^2 heta\).

label.en: ● All 6 Inverse Trigonometric Functions — Restricted Domains & Principal Ranges
label.ar: ● الدوال المثلثية العكسية الست جميعاً — المجالات المقيدة والمدى الأساسي

body.en:
Because the six trigonometric functions are periodic, they are not one-to-one on \(\mathbb{R}\). Restricting each forward function to its canonical principal branch makes it strictly monotonic so that a unique inverse exists (whose graph is the reflection of the restricted branch across \(y = x\)):

Inverse FunctionEquivalent StatementDomain of \(f^{-1}(x)\)Principal Range (Radians)Unit Circle Quadrants
\(y = \arcsin x = \sin^{-1} x\)\(\sin y = x\)\([-1, 1]\)\(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\)Quadrants IV & I
\(y = \arccos x = \cos^{-1} x\)\(\cos y = x\)\([-1, 1]\)\([0, \pi]\)Quadrants I & II
\(y = \arctan x = \tan^{-1} x\)\(\tan y = x\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\(\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\)Quadrants IV & I
\(y = \operatorname{arccsc} x = \csc^{-1} x\)\(\csc y = x\)\((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\)\(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, 0\right) \cup \left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\)Quadrants IV & I
\(y = \operatorname{arcsec} x = \sec^{-1} x\)\(\sec y = x\)\((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\)\(\left[0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right) \cup \left(\frac{\pi}{2}, \pi\right]\)Quadrants I & II
\(y = \operatorname{arccot} x = \cot^{-1} x\)\(\cot y = x\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((0, \pi)\)Quadrants I & II

Reciprocal & Cofunction Identities: \(\operatorname{arccsc}(x) = \arcsin(1/x)\) and \(\operatorname{arcsec}(x) = \arccos(1/x)\) for \(|x| \ge 1\); \(\arcsin x + \arccos x = \frac{\pi}{2}\) and \(\arctan x + \operatorname{arccot} x = \frac{\pi}{2}\).
body.ar:
نظراً لأن الدوال المثلثية الست دورية، فإنها ليست متباينة (واحداً لواحد) على \(\mathbb{R}\). بتقييد مجال كل دالة إلى فرعها الأساسي تصبح رتيبة تماماً وقابلة للعكس، ويكون تمثيل الدالة العكسية انعكاساً للفرع المقيّد حول المستقيم \(y = x\):

الدالة العكسيةالصيغة المكافئةمجال \(f^{-1}(x)\)المدى الأساسي (بالراديان)أرباع دائرة الوحدة
\(y = \arcsin x = \sin^{-1} x\)\(\sin y = x\)\([-1, 1]\)\(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\)الربعان الرابع والأول
\(y = \arccos x = \cos^{-1} x\)\(\cos y = x\)\([-1, 1]\)\([0, \pi]\)الربعان الأول والثاني
\(y = \arctan x = \tan^{-1} x\)\(\tan y = x\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\(\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\)الربعان الرابع والأول
\(y = \operatorname{arccsc} x = \csc^{-1} x\)\(\csc y = x\)\((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\)\(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, 0\right) \cup \left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\)الربعان الرابع والأول
\(y = \operatorname{arcsec} x = \sec^{-1} x\)\(\sec y = x\)\((-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty)\)\(\left[0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right) \cup \left(\frac{\pi}{2}, \pi\right]\)الربعان الأول والثاني
\(y = \operatorname{arccot} x = \cot^{-1} x\)\(\cot y = x\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((0, \pi)\)الربعان الأول والثاني

متطابقات المقلوبات والدوال المتممة: \(\operatorname{arccsc}(x) = \arcsin(1/x)\) و\(\operatorname{arcsec}(x) = \arccos(1/x)\) لكل \(|x| \ge 1\)؛ وكذلك \(\arcsin x + \arccos x = \frac{\pi}{2}\) و\(\arctan x + \operatorname{arccot} x = \frac{\pi}{2}\).
